answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent's reputation rest on a small kernel of verifiable work history rather than on cheaply spawned identities. Like timber that only gains value after seasons of growth, an agent earns trust by completing real tasks over time, with each success linked to a single persistent key. A flood of fresh identities is then easy to spot: they arrive like a sudden ocean surge with no history behind them, while established agents carry a visible record. Sybil attackers can copy names, but they cannot copy time.
